title: LibreDWG security-advisory crosswalk and generated negative-control readiness
mode: Primary-source web research with bounded local source/test inventory review
scope: Review current LibreDWG 0.14.1 parser-safety disclosures relevant to DWG decoding and object-graph staging.
Map decompression, page-map, record-loop, and pointer-lifetime failure shapes to existing libdxfrw paths and fast-test surfaces.
Refine the existing PAR-14 and PAR-07/S8 implementation readiness without promoting peer reports into local defects or support claims.

sources.revision: Public NEWS reviewed 2026-10-20; observations are from the v0.14 and v0.14.1 entries.
sources.observed: v0.14.1 records a second R2004 section-decompression heap overflow involving a buffer shrink while logical cursors remained larger, an unchecked R2004 page-map offset, pre-R2004 DXF VIEWPORT and MLINESTYLE pointer invalidation across object-array growth, and completion of a pre-R13 entity-end progress/resource fix. It also lists signed-count, NULL-check, and fuzz-discovered memory-safety fixes.
sources.limits: These are LibreDWG version-specific fixes. They identify useful adversarial shapes but do not show that libdxfrw has the same implementation or defects.

sources.project: LibreDWG R2004 section-decompression report and advisory
sources.revision: Public issue/advisory history reviewed 2026-10-20; release notes identify the v0.14.1 follow-up fix.
sources.observed: The report concerns heap-buffer overflow in the R2004 decompression path; release notes explain the later capacity-versus-logical-cursor shrink regression.
sources.limits: No issue PoC was downloaded or run; the report is not a libdxfrw reproduction.

sources.revision: Public GitHub Security Advisory reviewed 2026-10-20; advisory says affected versions are before 0.14 and the fix is in 0.14.
sources.observed: A crafted num_classes value caused uncontrolled allocation/slow-loop behavior in LibreDWG's decode_R13_R2000 path.
sources.limits: This is a peer-specific algorithmic-complexity report. It does not establish a corresponding defect in libdxfrw.

sources.revision: Public NEWS reviewed 2026-10-20; advisory identifiers and patched releases are recorded in the v0.14/v0.14.1 sections.
sources.observed: NEWS identifies a pre-R13 corrupt entities_end loop/resource fix, page-map range checking, and stale pointer use across object-array growth.
sources.limits: The libdxfrw AC1009/R11 reader is unsupported; peer pointer lifetime patterns are review prompts, not portable code-fix prescriptions.

localCrosswalk.observation: The decompressor takes an explicit output window, and the reader constructs page-local decoded storage and checks physical page ranges. Existing decompressor and reader-matrix tests provide fast coverage surfaces; adequacy for the exact peer capacity-versus-logical-size failure shape was not fully assessed.

localCrosswalk.surface: R2004/R2007 page-map offset and size admission
localCrosswalk.observation: Source contains checked arithmetic, file-range admission, and bounded map sizes; generated system-page/page-map probe infrastructure exists. Exact public-read refusal coverage remains an inventory task before adding tests.

localCrosswalk.surface: R13-R2000 class counts and parse progress
localCrosswalk.observation: Correction from the follow-up ODA-spec/source comparison: the R13-R15 section contains an RL payload size and class records are read to the payload boundary; it has no explicit num_classes field. The local parser bounds the payload by dwgSafety::MaxBufferSize, classNum is uint16_t (BS) with accepted values 500..65535, duplicate IDs are rejected, and DRW_Class::parseDwg must consume its mandatory fields before success. This is a different architecture from LibreDWG's per-record realloc trigger. No separate aggregate decoded-memory budget has been profiled; any such work is conditional on a shared-limit change or measured cost.

localCrosswalk.surface: Object pointer stability across graph mutation
localCrosswalk.observation: No direct equivalent was confirmed in this bounded review. Apply a local lifetime audit only where pointers/references into growable containers survive insertion, callbacks, or rehash.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-14: map peer safety reports to exact local reader paths and existing fast selectors before adding generated boundary mutations.
PAR-14: preserve checked arithmetic, bounded allocation/output windows, and record-loop progress; add only uncovered reachable invariants.
PAR-07/S8: keep malformed DataStorage handling and output transaction semantics distinct from DWG container/page-map safety.
Parser-safety checkpoint: use targeted ASan/UBSan or fuzz-harness validation at a composed milestone, not for every unrelated slice.
Fixture policy: use generated-from-scratch local bytes; do not download or commit the public peer PoC DWG.

planChanges: Added a research crosswalk for release-pinned LibreDWG decompression, page-map, class-count/progress, and object-pointer invalidation failure shapes.

Recorded existing libdxfrw bounded decode windows, checked page-map arithmetic/ranges, and generated test surfaces without asserting complete security coverage; the R13-R15 class path was later corrected to a section-payload plus class-ID-domain bound, not an explicit count ceiling.

Refined PAR-14/PAR-07 readiness to reuse existing fast tests, add only narrowly generated mutations for uncovered invariants, and consult the authoritative ODA specification before any DWG parse-body change.
Reaffirmed fast target plus focused CTest per change, less frequent full suites, no external PoC fixtures, self-unblocking when a peer/version is unavailable, and no support promotion.
limitations: LibreDWG release notes and advisories are peer evidence, not normative DWG format specifications or proof of a libdxfrw defect.
Local review was a bounded source/test inventory, not a full static-analysis, sanitizer, fuzz, or code audit.
No external drawing or advisory PoC was downloaded; no tests, peer binaries, native CAD applications, or geometry kernels were run.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain external-only, advisory, and non-promoting.
